learning_objective: 🎯 Give eyes to the machine! Understand how computers process images, recognize faces, and detect objects using grids of pixels.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Computers don't see images like we do; they only see numbers. Every digital image is made up of thousands of tiny squares called 'Pixels'. The computer reads the image as a giant grid (matrix) of numbers, where each number represents the color intensity of a pixel.

A Grayscale (black and white) image has only 1 channel of pixels, with values ranging from 0 (Black) to 255 (White). A Colored image has 3 channels: Red, Green, and Blue (RGB). The computer mixes these three matrices to create millions of colors.

Computer Vision is everywhere! It powers Face Unlock on smartphones, allows self-driving cars to detect pedestrians, helps doctors find tumors in X-rays, and is used in factories to detect defective products on an assembly line.

CNN is the specific deep learning algorithm used for Computer Vision. It passes 'filters' over an image to scan for features like edges, curves, and corners. Layer by layer, it combines these simple shapes to recognize complex objects like a dog or a car.

fun_activity.title: 🟩 The Pixel Grid Matrix
fun_activity.instructions: Take a piece of graph paper. Draw a smiley face by shading in whole squares (pixels) using only a black pen. You are mimicking exactly how a computer renders a 1-channel Grayscale image!

exam_tips: 📌 An image is stored in a computer as a matrix of numbers ranging from 0 to 255. 0 represents absolute Black, and 255 represents absolute White.
📌 Remember that RGB stands for Red, Green, and Blue. Colored images are 3D arrays (Height x Width x 3 channels).
📌 CNNs (Convolutional Neural Networks) are the standard algorithm for Computer Vision tasks. If a question asks about image processing, the answer is likely CNN.
quick_recap: ⭐ Computer Vision enables machines to derive meaningful information from digital images and videos.
⭐ Digital images are mathematically represented as matrices of pixel values.
⭐ CNNs extract features from images (like edges and textures) to classify them accurately.
